tools.playwright:
You have Microsoft Playwright for Python 1.62 (sync API) installed. Run a script by piping it to this interpreter:

"{PY}" - <<'EOF'
from playwright.sync_api import sync_playwright
with sync_playwright() as p:
    browser = p.chromium.launch(channel="msedge", headless=True)
    page = browser.new_page()
    ...
    browser.close()
EOF

It drives the installed Microsoft Edge. The whole Playwright sync API is available: page.goto, locators (get_by_role, get_by_label, locator(...)), locator.aria_snapshot() for an accessibility snapshot, fill, select_option, check, click, inner_text and evaluate. Each script starts a fresh browser, so do a whole flow inside one script.
tools.rustwright:
You have Rustwright 0.3 for Python installed: Playwright's API on a Rust engine, a drop-in for Playwright where only the import changes. Run a script by piping it to this interpreter, with the browser path set:

RUSTWRIGHT_CHROMIUM="{EDGE}" "{PY}" - <<'EOF'
from rustwright.sync_api import sync_playwright
with sync_playwright() as p:
    browser = p.chromium.launch(headless=True)
    page = browser.new_page()
    ...
    browser.close()
EOF

It drives the installed Microsoft Edge. The Playwright sync API is available: page.goto, locators (get_by_role, get_by_label, locator(...)), locator.aria_snapshot() for an accessibility snapshot, fill, select_option, check, click, inner_text and evaluate. Each script starts a fresh browser, so do a whole flow inside one script.
tools.caveman-browse:
You have caveman-browse 1.0 installed as a command-line tool. Every command needs the same environment, so run each one with this prefix:

CAVEMAN_HOME="{HOME}" CAVEMAN_BROWSE_PORT={PORT} CAVEMAN_BROWSE_CHROME="{EDGE}" "{CB}" <command>

Commands:
  snapshot <url> [query] [-i]
  act <uid> <click|type|select|scroll|wait> [text or option]
  eval "<javascript expression>"
  recover <handle> [query]
  close

These are the command-line forms of the four tools in its own guide, quoted below. Two differences from the guide, which describes the MCP server: on the command line, snapshot always navigates to the url, so it reloads the page and clears anything typed into it; and the browser stays open between commands until you run close. It drives the installed Microsoft Edge. Run close when you finish.

notes: Each tool gets its own agent-facing documentation. Playwright needs none quoted: the model already knows it. caveman-browse is new, so its official guide is quoted, as its plugin would inject it.
The two command-line differences stated in the caveman-browse card were measured, not assumed: a snapshot without a url attaches to a blank target, and a snapshot with the url reloads the page.
Every run gets its own CAVEMAN_HOME and port, so concurrent caveman-browse runs cannot share a session.
